source_evidence: Stock funds invest primarily in stocks or equities.
answer: Stock funds and bond funds differ mainly in what they invest in. A stock fund invests primarily in stocks, which represent ownership interests in companies. Its value can rise or fall quickly, and its performance depends on how the underlying companies do. A bond fund invests primarily in bonds or other debt securities. The bonds it holds can vary in risk, return, duration, and volatility. So, the label tells you the fund’s main type of investment, but funds within either category can have different characteristics.
